To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the management of New Commons is a drama, not a tragedy.
the plurality of stakeholders and values, coupled with the spatial scale mismatches, are the root causes of the tragedy of the New Commons.

mismatches in the spatial scales at different levels of the ecosystem service supply chain (from the production of the service, its distribution and its consumption) create challenges in managing the New Commons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the New Commons are managed and how this management can be improved.
the management of the mismatches in the provision of ecosystem services at the New Commons scale.
the spatial mismatches in the production and consumption of ecosystem services, and the institutional arrangements that govern their use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the New Commons is a complex system that requires a multi-disciplinary approach to address and that the management of these commons is a complex drama with many actors at many scales and with many values.

the New Commons is a complex system of interacting and interdependent processes that are organized in space and time, and that the management of these processes and the resources that they provide is dependent on a plurality of values and institutions that operate at different scales and are often in conflict with each other.
there are mismatches at multiple levels and scales in the management of ecosystem services for human wellbeing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the New Commons are a mosaic of land and water and their underlying processes which provide ecosystem goods and services to human well-being.
the New Commons are not a tragedy but a drama that is dependent on the interplay of the multiple scales and the multiple values of ecosystem services.

the management of ecosystem services is not only a matter of the management of common property resources, but also a matter of the mismanagement of common property resources due to mismatches between the spatial scales of the production and consumption of ecosystem services, and the spatial scales of institutions and stakeholders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the New Commons is a complex system that requires an integrated understanding of the interactions among the various scales at which ecosystem services and their underlying processes are provided.
the mismatches in the provision of ecosystem services are not just a matter of scale.
the mismatches between the spatial scales at different levels of ecosystem management are the key to understanding the New Commons.
